newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares extend fall, seen down on Monday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares extend fall, seen down on Monday.

text.p: Polish shares extended Thursday's falls and analysts said the market was undergoing a profit-taking correction after its previous four-session, 2.7-percent rise seen linked with gains on major western bourses.
Analysts said the market, currently at 14,920.4 points, could slip below 14,800 points before picking up toward the middle of next week before firms release their September earnings reports.
"It looks like we'll have falls for a few sessions, with the first support line at 14,800 points possibly broken," said Grzegorz Pindur, an analyst at Bank Staropolski brokerage.
The main market's all-share WIG index fell 0.9 percent to 14,920.4 points and turnover fell 22.7 percent to 108.9 million zlotys on both markets.
Analysts said biggest loser Paged, which fell 6.7 percent in active trade, was hit by profit-taking after having started trade on Thursday 50 percent above issue.

Continuous trade turnover was at 1.1 million zlotys with biggest mover Universal down 1.8 percent. NFI units fell 1.2 percent in a 40-million-zloty turnover and fell 0.9 percent in 13.7-million-zloty continuous trade.
